chapters.title: 2.1 Test Structure Syntax
chapters.overviewText: Cypress specs are Mocha: describe/context group tests, it/specify name cases, and before/beforeEach/after/afterEach run hooks. Because testIsolation defaults to true since Cypress 12, shared login belongs in beforeEach (later: cy.session), not a one-shot before. Use a function () callback—not an arrow—when you need Mocha's this.skip() or this.aliasName. This chapter is the grammar of every HRM spec you will write.
chapters.why: Arrow functions silently break this.skip and alias access via this. Isolation makes before-only login a false pattern that flakes or fails after Cypress 12. Interviewers watch whether your skeleton would survive a second it() in the same file.
chapters.when: Starting every spec, when a second test 'cannot see' the dashboard, when you want to skip on a condition, and when migrating suites that logged in once in before().

practical.scenario: You need two tests: employee submits leave, manager sees it pending. Both require a logged-in session, and one should skip if Cypress.env('featureLeave') is false.
practical.pass: You use describe/it, beforeEach to visit/login (isolation), and a function () { if (!flag) this.skip(); } — not an arrow, not a single before() that the second test depends on.
practical.fail: You login in before() only, write async () => { await cy.visit }, or this.skip() inside an arrow function and wonder why this is empty.

chapters.customSummary:
- Mocha: describe/context, it/specify, before, beforeEach, after, afterEach — Cypress does not use Jest's test() as the primary API.
- testIsolation true (Cypress 12+): cookies/storage cleared between tests → beforeEach (or cy.session) is required for login, not optional style.
- Use function () {} when you need this.skip(), this.timeout(), or this.alias from .as().
- Arrows are fine when you do not use Mocha this — most HRM tests can stay arrows until they need skip/alias-on-this.
- only/skip: it.only, it.skip, describe.skip — never leave only on main.
- Hooks run in a defined order; avoid cy.visit in afterEach unless you are cleaning a side effect you own.

chapters.title: 2.2 cy.visit, cy.get, cy.contains, cy.find
chapters.overviewText: cy.visit loads a URL in the AUT iframe. cy.get queries from the document root by selector. cy.contains finds by text (optionally scoped to a selector). cy.find searches descendants of the previous subject and cannot be used as cy.find from a blank chain. Choosing among get/contains/find is the daily locator skill; mixing them wrong yields 'must be chained' errors or overly broad matches.
chapters.why: get vs find is the first Cypress-specific locator question in interviews. contains is how you click 'Submit' without a brittle CSS class. visit without baseUrl or without waiting via a following assertion is how smoke tests lie.
chapters.when: Every spec. Revisit when cy.find throws, when contains matches a hidden template, and when you are tempted to CSS-select by text.

practical.scenario: On /leave, click the Submit button inside the request form without matching a different Submit in the nav, then assert a table row that contains Ada Lovelace.
practical.fail: You call cy.find('button') with no parent, or cy.get('button') and click the first of six, or cy.contains('Ada') matching a toast and a row.

chapters.customSummary:
- cy.visit(path|url) uses baseUrl for relative paths; waits for load (pageLoadTimeout), not for your SPA fetch.
- cy.get(selector) queries the whole document (or within a cy.within); retries until it exists.
- cy.contains(text) or cy.contains(selector, text) queries by content; more user-like than CSS.
- cy.find(selector) must be chained off a subject — descendants only. Never cy.find() at the root.
- Prefer get(form).find(button) or contains('button', 'Submit') over get('button') when duplicates exist.
- Playwright: page.goto / locator / getByText / locator.locator. Selenium: get / findElement / XPath contains().
chapters.contentMarkdown:
## `cy.visit` — enter the app

```ts
cy.visit('/leave/new');                 // baseUrl + path
cy.visit('https://staging.example/leave/new'); // absolute, ignores baseUrl prefix
cy.visit('/leave', { qs: { tab: 'pending' } });
cy.visit('/leave', {
  onBeforeLoad(win) {
    // too early for most tests; intercepts are usually enough
  },
});
```

`visit` waits for the window **`load`** event (see `pageLoadTimeout`, default 60s). A React HRM page can `load` while a spinner still shows. **The next assertion** is what waits for UI readiness:

```ts
cy.visit('/leave');
cy.get('[data-cy=leave-table]').should('be.visible');
```

Do not follow visit with `cy.wait(3000)`.

Options you will actually use:

| Option | Why |
|---|---|
| `failOnStatusCode: false` | Visit an expected 404 page |
| `timeout` | One slow cold compile |
| `headers` | Rare; prefer `cy.session` / intercept |
| `qs` | Query string object |

Playwright: `page.goto` waits for `load`/`domcontentloaded`/`networkidle` by option. Cypress does not have `networkidle` as a visit wait — use intercepts (`cy.wait('@alias')`) or UI assertions.

Selenium: `driver.get` — no SPA wait at all unless you add WebDriverWait.

## `cy.get` — CSS/selector from the root

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=leave-table]');
cy.get('#email');
cy.get('.btn-primary'); // brittle; last resort
```

`cy.get` always starts from the **root document** of the AUT (unless you are inside `cy.within`). It is **not** "get relative to last element" — that is `find`.

```ts
cy.get('form').get('button'); // second get is STILL the whole document's buttons
cy.get('form').find('button'); // buttons inside that form
```

This is the #1 `get` vs `find` bug.

`cy.get` retries until at least one element matches or `defaultCommandTimeout` (4s) elapses. It yields a **jQuery collection** (all matches, not only the first) as the subject. Actions like `.click()` use the **first** matched element unless you `.eq(n)` / `.last()`.

```ts
cy.get('button');              // might match 12 buttons
cy.get('button').eq(0).click(); // explicit first
cy.get('button').should('have.length', 1).click(); // fail if duplicates
```

Prefer unique `data-cy` in HRM components:

```html
<button data-cy="leave-submit" type="submit">Submit</button>
```

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=leave-submit]').click();
```

## `cy.contains` — by text

```ts
cy.contains('Sign in');
cy.contains('button', 'Sign in');
cy.contains(/pending/i);
cy.contains('[data-cy=status]', 'Pending');
```

Signatures:

- `cy.contains(content)`
- `cy.contains(selector, content)`
- Chained: `cy.get('table').contains('td', 'Ada Lovelace')`

`contains` finds the **deepest** element that has the text, which is usually what you want for a click. It still retries.

**Scope it** when the string appears twice:

```ts
cy.contains('Submit'); // nav + form + modal?
cy.get('[data-cy=leave-form]').contains('button', 'Submit').click();
cy.contains('[data-cy=leave-form] button', 'Submit').click();
```

`cy.contains('button', 'Submit')` is "a button whose content includes Submit" — better than `cy.get('button').contains('Submit')` in some chains; both appear in the wild.

Hidden text: `contains` can match elements that are not visible. Follow with `.should('be.visible')` before clicking, or the click will retry on **actionability** (2.4).

Playwright: `getByText`, `getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' })`. Cypress 12+ has `cy.get` + selector playground; `cy.contains` is still the text tool. There is no first-class `getByRole` in core Cypress (Testing Library plugins exist — optional).

Selenium: `By.xpath("//button[contains(., 'Submit')]")` — `contains` is the readable version of that.

## `cy.find` — descendants of the current subject

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=leave-form]').find('input[name=startDate]');
cy.get('table tbody').find('tr').should('have.length', 3);
```

**`cy.find` cannot start a chain.**

```ts
cy.find('button'); // CypressError: must be chained off a previous command
```

`find` uses jQuery `.find()`: descendants, not the subject element itself. If the subject *is* the button, `find('button')` is empty. Use `.filter` / `.closest` / get the parent first.

| Command | Starts from | Relative? | Root OK? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cy.get` | Document (or `within` root) | No | Yes `cy.get` |
| `cy.contains` | Document or previous subject if chained | Optional | Yes `cy.contains` |
| `.find` | Previous subject | Yes, descendants | **No** |

## `cy.within` — temporary root for `get`

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=leave-form]').within(() => {
  cy.get('input[name=startDate]').type('2026-09-21');
  cy.get('input[name=endDate]').type('2026-09-21');
  cy.contains('button', 'Submit').click();
});
```

Inside `within`, `cy.get` is scoped to that element. `find` is still chained. `within` is how you avoid repeating the form selector. Do not nest `within` deeply — readability dies.

## Decision table (HRM)

| Intent | Command |
|---|---|
| Load the leave page | `cy.visit('/leave')` |
| Unique `data-cy` | `cy.get('[data-cy=leave-table]')` |
| Click labeled button | `cy.contains('button', 'Approve')` |
| CSS inside a known parent | `cy.get('[data-cy=row-12]').find('.status')` |
| Several fields in one card | `cy.get('[data-cy=leave-form]').within(() => { ... })` |
| Row that shows a name | `cy.contains('tr', 'Ada Lovelace')` |

## Playwright / Selenium mapping

| Cypress | Playwright | Selenium |
|---|---|---|
| `cy.visit` | `page.goto` | `driver.get` |
| `cy.get(sel)` | `page.locator(sel)` | `findElement(By.css)` |
| `cy.contains(text)` | `getByText` / `getByRole` | XPath text |
| `.find(sel)` | `locator.locator(sel)` | `element.findElement` |
| `.within` | `locator` scoped variable | search context element |

Playwright locators are **lazy** and re-query; Cypress `get` also re-queries while retrying. Selenium `WebElement` goes **stale**. Cypress/Playwright win here.

## Common errors

1. **`cy.find` at root** — use `cy.get`.
2. **`cy.get('form').get('input')`** — second get is global; use `find` or `within`.
3. **`cy.contains('Ada')` on a page listing Ada in nav, toast, and table** — scope to `tr` or `data-cy`.
4. **Visit and immediately `cy.get` a list that is fetched** — assertion retries; if 4s is tight, intercept + `cy.wait('@alias')` (Part 5), not a longer global timeout.
5. **`.get('div')`** — too wide; Command Log will show 200 matches.

## Small HRM example combining all four

```ts
it('submits leave from the new-request page', () => {
  cy.visit('/leave/new');
  cy.get('[data-cy=leave-form]').within(() => {
    cy.get('[name=startDate]').type('2026-09-21');
    cy.find('[name=endDate]').type('2026-09-21'); // chained inside within's subject
    cy.contains('button', 'Submit').click();
  });
  cy.contains('[data-cy=toast]', 'Request submitted').should('be.visible');
});
```

Next: how these commands **chain**, and why the queue is two-phase.
## `cy.visit` options you will touch later

```ts
cy.visit('/login', {
  failOnStatusCode: true,
  retryOnStatusCodeFailure: false,
  retryOnNetworkFailure: true,
});
```

Auth cookies: prefer `cy.session` (later) over stuffing `onBeforeLoad` with `localStorage.setItem('token')` unless the app truly stores tokens that way.

Query strings:

```ts
cy.visit({ url: '/leave', qs: { filter: 'pending', page: '2' } });
```

## `cy.get` vs jQuery vs `Cypress.$`

`Cypress.$('button')` is **synchronous jQuery** with **no retry**. Only use it inside `.then` after the page is ready. Day-to-day: `cy.get`.

```ts
cy.get('body').then(($body) => {
  const n = $body.find('[data-cy=row]').length; // snapshot
});
```

## `contains` regex and whitespace

```ts
cy.contains(/sign\s*in/i);
cy.contains('button', /^Submit$/);
```

HRM copy that includes extra spaces or NBSP fails exact `'have.text'`. `contains` is more forgiving. Still scope to a selector when the word "Submit" is everywhere.

## `find` vs `children` vs `eq`

```ts
cy.get('tr').eq(2);          // 3rd row, 0-based, among all tr
cy.get('tbody').find('tr').eq(2);
cy.get('ul').children('li'); // direct children only
```

`find` is descendants (all depths). `children` is one level. Wrong one is a common "element not found" on nested HRM tables.

## `within` gotcha

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=leave-form]').within(() => {
  cy.visit('/other'); // AUT navigates; within scope is now nonsense
});
```

Do not visit inside `within`. Keep `within` to filling a form.

## Interview drill

Why is `cy.get('form').get('input')` wrong? When does `cy.find` throw? How do you click the Submit that is in the form, not the nav? What does `visit` wait for, and what does it not wait for?
## `cy.get` alias of jQuery selectors

```ts
cy.get('input[name=email]');
cy.get('.modal:visible');      // :visible is jQuery — works, but prefer should('be.visible')
cy.get('[data-cy^=leave-]');   // prefix match
```

`:visible` in the selector is a snapshot of CSS, not the same retry story as `.should('be.visible')`. Prefer assertion.

## Contains + get combo errors

```ts
cy.get('button').contains('Submit').click();
```

This works (chain contains off get). It clicks a button among the matched buttons that has that text. Equivalent scoped form:

```ts
cy.contains('button', 'Submit').click();
```

Prefer the latter; fewer ways to accidentally click a `div` that contains a button.

## Visiting `about:blank` between tests

With isolation, you always `visit` in the test or `beforeEach`. A helper `cy.login` should end on a known page or not visit until the test asks. Double visit (login visits `/`, test visits `/leave`) is OK and clearer than clever reuse.

## `cy.go` and `cy.reload`

```ts
cy.go('back');
cy.reload();
```

Both are load-ish commands (`pageLoadTimeout`). They are not substitutes for `visit` in smoke tests. Use reload when testing "refetch on refresh."

## Selector Playground vs `data-cy`

Playground may suggest `nth-child`. Do not paste that into HRM specs. Add `data-cy="leave-submit"` on the component. Playwright's `getByTestId` is the same idea (`data-testid`). Selenium has no standard; teams invent `data-test`.
## `cy.root()` inside `within`

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=leave-form]').within(() => {
  cy.root().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'leave-form');
  cy.get('input').should('have.length.at.least', 2);
});
```

`cy.root()` is the current within subject. `cy.get` stays scoped. `cy.find` still needs a previous chained subject (`cy.root().find('input')` is equivalent to `cy.get('input')` here).

## `prev`, `next`, `parent` (use sparingly)

```ts
cy.contains('td', 'Ada Lovelace').parent('tr').find('[data-cy=status]');
```

This is a valid alternative to `cy.contains('tr', 'Ada Lovelace')`. Prefer the latter. Traversal commands (`parent`, `next`, `siblings`) retry as part of the chain when followed by `should`.
## `cy.get` timeout vs visit timeout

A visit that never `load`s fails with `pageLoadTimeout` (60s), not 4s. A get that never matches fails at 4s. Reading the error title tells you which layer (Part 1.5) to touch — still prefer a better assertion over a bigger number.

## Contains from a previous subject

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=leave-table]').contains('tr', 'Ada Lovelace');
```

This is `contains` **chained**, scoped to the table. Equivalent spirit to `get(table).find('tr').contains('Ada')` but `contains('tr', text)` finds a `tr` that has the text, which is usually the row you wanted.
## `hash` visits

```ts
cy.visit('/leave#pending');
cy.hash().should('eq', '#pending');
```

If HRM routing is path-based (Next.js), you will use `pathname` more than `hash`. Visit still waits for `load`; the client router may then replace the URL — assert `location` after.

chapters.title: 2.3 Chaining & the Command Queue
chapters.overviewText: Cypress is a two-phase engine: phase 1 runs your it() body synchronously and enqueues Chainables; phase 2 executes the queue in order, passing a subject down the chain. Chaining is how get().find().should().click() shares one query-and-retry pipeline. You must never await cy.* and never treat a Chainable as a resolved value. .then() hops into a callback when a command finishes; it does not turn Cypress into Promises.
chapters.why: Almost every 'Cypress is broken' Slack thread is a queue misunderstanding: awaiting, assigning, or breaking the chain so retries stop. If you can draw enqueue vs execute on a whiteboard, you can debug anything in Parts 3–6.
chapters.when: Writing any spec, converting Playwright tests, using .then to read text, and whenever you are tempted to put Cypress commands inside Promise.all or a for-loop of awaits.

practical.scenario: You need the leave balance text, then type a date, then click Submit — and a teammate's PR uses await cy.get and const text = cy.get('.balance').invoke('text').
practical.pass: You chain or use .then(($el) => { ... cy.wrap / further cy commands }); you explain two-phase enqueue/execute; you reject await cy.get.
practical.fail: You await cy.get('.balance'), or store the chainable in a const and read .text() immediately, or mix async/await with the queue.

chapters.customSummary:
- Two-phase: (1) it() runs sync and enqueues commands; (2) Cypress executes the queue with retry.
- Never await cy.* — Chainables are not Promises you should await (manual rule even where thenable).
- A chain passes a subject: get → find → should → click. Breaking the chain starts a new root command (cy.get).
- .then(cb) runs when the previous command yields; commands inside then are also enqueued. .then itself does not retry (2.4).
- Synchronous JS loops enqueue N commands immediately; they do not wait between iterations unless you chain.
- Playwright await is correct there; copying that pattern into Cypress is the migration bug.

chapters.title: 2.4 Retry-ability
chapters.overviewText: Cypress retries queries and assertions together until they pass or defaultCommandTimeout fires. Retry is driven by assertions: get().should('have.length', 3) re-queries until three rows exist, then the chain continues. Clicks and type wait for actionability (visible, enabled, not covered, not animating), while .then() never retries. This chapter is the difference between Cypress and a Selenium implicit wait, and between Cypress should and a Playwright expect.
chapters.why: Flakes are usually assertions that were written as .then, clicks that miss actionability, or global timeouts used as a blunt instrument. Interviews: 'what does Cypress retry?' — not 'everything', and not '.then'.
chapters.when: Any time a list populates asynchronously, a button is covered by a spinner, or a test passes only with cy.wait(ms). Also when converting expect() in a then() that needed to retry.

practical.scenario: The leave table is empty, then three rows arrive from GET /api/leave. You must click the last row once all three exist, without a fixed wait.
practical.pass: cy.get('[data-cy=leave-table] tbody tr').should('have.length', 3).last().click(); you know .then(($rows) => expect($rows).to.have.length(3)) would flake; you wait for actionability on the click.
practical.fail: You cy.wait(2000), or assert length inside .then, or click before the overlay spinner is gone and disable retry by wrapping in .then.

chapters.customSummary:
- Retry is assertion-driven: should/and retry the preceding query until pass or timeout.
- Actions retry until actionability: visible, enabled, not disabled, not covered, not animating.
- .then() never retries — snapshot the subject once. Put retryable checks in .should.
- defaultCommandTimeout (4s) bounds DOM retries; do not raise it globally (Part 1.5).
- cy.wait(ms) is not retry-ability. cy.wait('@alias') waits on network, then UI still needs should.
- Playwright expect(locator) retries similarly; Selenium implicit wait does not retry assertions.
chapters.contentMarkdown:
## Retry is not "Cypress waits 4 seconds then clicks"

A command **re-runs its query** (and its assertion, if any) until:

- the assertion passes, or
- the command's timeout hits (`defaultCommandTimeout` 4000 ms unless overridden)

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=leave-table] tbody tr')
  .should('have.length', 3)
  .last()
  .click();
```

Timeline:

1. `get` finds 0 rows → `should` fails internally → **retry get + should**
2. 1 row appears → still fail → retry
3. 3 rows → `should` passes → subject is the 3 rows → `.last()` → `.click()`

`.click()` then applies **actionability** retries (covered below).

Without `should('have.length', 3)`, `get('tr').last().click()` might click the only row that exists at t=0, then the table re-renders — flake. **The assertion is what defines the wait.**

## Assertions drive retries

| Pattern | Retries? |
|---|---|
| `cy.get('.x').should('be.visible')` | Yes — query + assertion |
| `cy.get('.x').should('have.length', 3)` | Yes |
| `cy.get('.x').and('contain.text', 'Ada')` | Yes (`and` is `should`) |
| `cy.contains('Ada').should('exist')` | Yes |
| `cy.get('.x').then(($el) => { expect($el).to.have.length(3); })` | **No** |
| `cy.get('.x').should(($el) => { expect($el).to.have.length(3); })` | **Yes** (function assertion) |

The `.then` vs `.should` distinction is the most important in this chapter.

```ts
// FLAKY — then does not retry
cy.get('tr').then(($rows) => {
  expect($rows).to.have.length(3);
});

// STABLE — should retries
cy.get('tr').should('have.length', 3);

// STABLE — should with function still retries the get
cy.get('tr').should(($rows) => {
  expect($rows.length).to.eq(3);
});
```

Inside a `.should(fn)`, throwing (or failing `expect`) triggers retry. Do not `cy.*` inside `.should(fn)` — Cypress documents that as unsupported. Use `.then` for nested commands.

## `.then` never retries

`.then` means: **the previous command has yielded; run this callback once.**

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=status]').then(($el) => {
  const text = $el.text(); // snapshot NOW
  expect(text).to.eq('Pending'); // if still "Loading", fail immediately
});
```

Use `.then` for:

- branching (`if`)
- parsing once you already `.should`'d readiness
- kicking off more `cy` commands after a guaranteed subject

Do not use `.then` as a waiting assertion.

## Actionability (clicks, type, check, select)

Before `.click()`, `.type()`, `.clear()`, `.check()`, Cypress asserts the element is **actionable**:

- **visible** (not `display:none`, not zero size, not `visibility:hidden` in the Cypress sense)
- **not disabled** (`disabled` attribute / `aria-disabled` depending on command)
- **not covered** by another element (spinner overlay, modal backdrop, sticky header)
- **not animating** (waits for animation to finish)
- inside a scrollable container: Cypress **scrolls it into view**

If a spinner covers **Submit**, `.click()` retries until the spinner is gone or timeout. The error is famous:

```text
cy.click() failed because this element is being covered by another element:
<div class="spinner-overlay">...
```

Fix the overlay (or `cy.get('[data-cy=leave-table]').should('be.visible')` first), do not `{ force: true }` by habit. `force: true` skips actionability — valid for hidden file inputs, a last resort otherwise.

Playwright also has actionability (visible, stable, enabled, receives events). Selenium clicks the coordinates the driver has — **no** cover check. Cypress/Playwright catch "click intercepted" class bugs; Selenium often "clicks" the overlay.

## Timeouts: layered, local first

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=payroll-grid]', { timeout: 15000 }).should('be.visible');
```

Per-command `timeout` overrides `defaultCommandTimeout` for **that** command. Visit uses `pageLoadTimeout`. Tasks use `taskTimeout`.

**Never** set `defaultCommandTimeout: 30000` in config to make this grid pass (Part 1.5). You hide locator bugs in every other command.

## What does *not* retry

| Command / pattern | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `.then()` | Once |
| `.spread()` | Once |
| Most `cy.wrap(plainObject)` + immediate sync read | No DOM retry unless `.should` is attached |
| `cy.wait(1000)` | Sleep, then continue |
| `expect(x).to.eq(1)` in the `it` body (phase 1) | Runs before the app exists — useless |
| `cy.request` | HTTP; not DOM retry (has its own request/response timeouts) |

`cy.wrap($el).should('have.class', 'ready')` **does** retry if `$el` is a DOM/jQuery subject that Cypress can re-query — wrap of a **detached snapshot** may not re-query. Prefer `cy.get` over wrapping a stale node.

## `cy.wait` vs retry-ability

```ts
cy.wait(5000);                 // always 5s — slow and still racy
cy.wait('@getLeave');          // wait for intercept alias (Part 5)
cy.get('tr').should('have.length', 3); // wait for UI truth
```

Best HRM pattern: intercept the list API, `cy.wait('@getLeave')`, **then** `should('have.length', n)` if you still care about render. Network done ≠ DOM painted.

## Playwright / Selenium comparison

| | Cypress | Playwright | Selenium |
|---|---|---|---|
| Retry assertions | `should` with the query | `expect(locator).toHaveCount(3)` | Manual `WebDriverWait` + ExpectedConditions |
| Click cover check | Yes (actionability) | Yes | No (usually) |
| Non-retrying hook | `.then` | reading `await locator.count()` without expect can be a snapshot | `findElements` size now |
| Global implicit wait | Discouraged (`defaultCommandTimeout` keep 4s) | `timeout` in config, still used more narrowly | Implicit wait — classic footgun |

Playwright's `await expect(locator).toHaveCount(3)` is the cousin of `cy.get().should('have.length', 3)`. Playwright's `await locator.count()` **without** expect is the cousin of `.then` — a snapshot.

## HRM example: spinner then table

```ts
it('shows three leave rows after load', () => {
  cy.visit('/leave');
  cy.get('[data-cy=leave-table] tbody tr')
    .should('have.length', 3)
    .last()
    .find('[data-cy=open]')
    .click();
  cy.contains('h1', 'Leave detail').should('be.visible');
});
```

If the click still fails as covered:

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=spinner]').should('not.exist');
```

That assertion retries until the spinner is gone — then click.

## Debugging retries in the GUI

The Command Log shows a **pinwheel** on the command while it retries, then a match count. Click the command: see the DOM at attempts. If it "tried for 4s and 0 matched", your selector is wrong. If it matched 1 then 3, you needed `have.length`.

Next: **aliases** — naming subjects, intercepts, and data so later commands can reuse them without illegal `const`.
## Retry diagram (leave table)

```text
t=0ms   get tr → 0 nodes → should length 3 fail → retry
t=200   get tr → 0 nodes (spinner) → retry
t=800   get tr → 3 nodes → should pass → last() → click
t=800+  click waits until not covered by spinner
```

If you had used `.then(expect length 3)` at t=0, the test fails immediately.

## `{ timeout, interval }`

```ts
cy.get('tr', { timeout: 10000, interval: 200 }).should('have.length', 3);
```

`interval` is how often Cypress re-queries (default ~50–60ms). You almost never change it. You sometimes change `timeout`.

## `force: true` catalog

Acceptable: `<input type="file">` hidden, custom widgets that never become "visible" but are the real control. Unacceptable: covering modal, disabled button, off-screen tab you should open first.

## Animations

Cypress waits for CSS animations to finish (actionability). If HRM uses perpetual skeleton shimmer, actionability may wait until `defaultCommandTimeout`. Assert `data-cy=table-ready` or wait for intercept instead of clicking the shimmer.

## `cy.clock` interaction (preview)

If you freeze clocks, animations and timeouts in the **app** may never finish. Actionability can then hang. Unlock the clock before clicking, or do not freeze for that spec.

## Interview drill

What drives retry? Does `.then` retry? Name four actionability checks. How do you wait for 3 rows then click the last? Why not `cy.wait(2000)`?
## `should('exist')` after get is weak

`cy.get('.x')` already retries until the element exists. Adding `.should('exist')` rarely changes the wait. Adding `.should('be.visible')` or length/text **does**.

## Request vs DOM retry

`cy.wait('@getLeave')` retries until the intercept fires (`requestTimeout` / wait timeout). It does not retry your table assertion. Always follow with a DOM `should` if the user cares about rows.

## Flake recipe and the fix

Recipe: click Submit, `then` read toast text, `expect` equals Saved. Toast appears at 300ms; `then` ran at 20ms. Fix: `cy.contains('[data-cy=toast]', 'Saved').should('be.visible')`.

## `{ force: true }` on type

`cy.get('input').type('x', { force: true })` types even if covered. You may hide that a date picker overlay is eating clicks. Prefer closing the overlay.

## Comparison sentence for interviews

"Cypress retries the **query plus assertion** until timeout; `.then` is a snapshot. Playwright retries `expect(locator)`. Selenium retries only if I wrote a wait. Actionability means Cypress refuses to click covered/disabled/animating elements."
## `defaultCommandTimeout` vs assertion message

When a `should('have.length', 3)` fails, the error includes "tried for 4000ms" (or your timeout). That number is the knob you overrode — or the global you should **not** have raised. Read it before editing config.

## `cy.get` with `{ timeout: 0 }`

```ts
cy.get('.toast', { timeout: 0 }).should('not.exist');
```

Zero timeout means one attempt. Useful after you already waited for a positive signal and want a cheap negative check. Dangerous as a first assertion on a slow page.

## Covered-by error — HRM spinner

Leave table specs should either wait for `[data-cy=leave-table]` visible **and** `[data-cy=spinner]` not exist, or `should('have.length', n)` on rows (rows imply spinner gone if the UI is built that way). Know which your frontend does.
## `should('be.visible')` vs opacity 0

A modal with `opacity: 0` may still "exist." Cypress visibility rules are documented (no zero size, no `display:none`, not `visibility:hidden`, not covered — coverage is actionability for clicks more than `be.visible`). If a designer uses opacity animations, assert a `data-state=open` attribute the component already has.
## `requestTimeout` on `cy.wait('@alias')`

If the intercept never fires, you wait until the wait timeout (related to `requestTimeout`), not `defaultCommandTimeout`. Wrong layer again. Register the intercept **before** `visit`.
## Summary card

Retry = query + `should`/`and`/`should(fn)` + actionability on actions. No retry = `.then`, phase-1 `expect`, `cy.wait(ms)`. Fix flakes with a better assertion, an intercept wait, or a local `{ timeout }`, never a 30s global `defaultCommandTimeout`.

chapters.title: 2.5 Aliases
chapters.overviewText: Aliases are Cypress's answer to const. There are three kinds: DOM (cy.get(...).as('rows')), intercept/route (cy.intercept(...).as('getLeave')), and data (cy.wrap/fixture().as('user')). You retrieve with cy.get('@name') or, in function () callbacks after the alias command has run, this.name. Aliases are not JavaScript variables; they are named slots on the queue.
chapters.why: Saving cy.get in a const does not work (queue). Aliases are the supported pattern for reuse, for cy.wait('@alias'), and for fixtures. Mixing up the three kinds — waiting on a DOM alias, or this.user in an arrow function — is a frequent live-coding miss.
chapters.when: When you need the same element twice, when stubbing/waiting on XHR, when loading fixtures, and when sharing data between beforeEach and it via this.

practical.scenario: Stub GET /api/leave as getLeave, fixture employees as employees, and reuse the leave table rows to assert length then click the last row.
practical.pass: You use three aliases: intercept.as('getLeave') + cy.wait('@getLeave'); cy.fixture('employees.json').as('employees') + function () { this.employees }; cy.get('tr').as('rows') + cy.get('@rows').should('have.length', 3).
practical.fail: You const rows = cy.get('tr'), or cy.wait('@rows') on a DOM alias, or this.employees inside an arrow it().

chapters.customSummary:
- Three alias kinds: (1) DOM subjects, (2) intercept/route aliases for cy.wait('@name'), (3) data (fixtures, wrap, request bodies).
- Create with .as('camelCase'). Read DOM/data with cy.get('@camelCase'); wait on intercepts with cy.wait('@camelCase').
- this.alias works only in function () callbacks after the alias command has executed (typically next hook/test).
- DOM aliases re-query when used with cy.get('@name') in modern Cypress (avoid stale elements).
- Do not cy.wait on a DOM alias. Do not treat .as as assigning a JS const.
- Playwright: no exact alias; use variables + await, waitForResponse, fixtures file API.

chapters.title: 2.6 Assertions — implicit vs explicit
chapters.overviewText: Implicit assertions are .should() / .and() on a chain — they retry with the query. Explicit assertions are expect(...) from Chai, typically inside .then() or a should(callback) — expect by itself does not retry a cy.get. Cypress ships Chai, Chai-jQuery, and Sinon-Chai. Prefer should for anything that waits on the DOM; use expect for already-resolved values (status codes, parsed JSON, math).
chapters.why: Writing expect($el.text()).to.eq('Pending') inside .then is the classic flake. Writing should('exist') on every line is noise. Interviews want: should retries, expect does not (unless wrapped in should(fn)).
chapters.when: After every command that needs a pass/fail meaning, when asserting API bodies, and when a teammate's Chai-jQuery chain fails to compile in TS.

practical.scenario: Assert the leave table has 3 visible rows labeled Pending, and that a cy.request to /api/health returned { ok: true }.
practical.pass: DOM: cy.get('tr').should('have.length', 3).and('be.visible'); rows cy.contains('Pending'). Request: .its('body').should('deep.include', { ok: true }) or .then((r) => expect(r.body.ok).to.eq(true)).
practical.fail: You cy.get('tr').then($tr => expect($tr).to.have.length(3)) as the only wait, or you expect in the it body before visit.

chapters.customSummary:
- Implicit: .should('be.visible') / .and(...) — retries with the previous query.
- Explicit: expect(value).to.eq(...) — Chai; no retry unless inside .should(fn).
- Chai-jQuery: have.class, have.attr, contain.text, be.checked, have.length.
- should('exist') is often redundant after get; prefer user-visible assertions (text, length, enabled).
- .should(fn) retries; do not nest cy.* inside it. .then + expect does not retry.
- Playwright expect(locator) retries; Selenium Assert does not wait.
chapters.contentMarkdown:
## Implicit vs explicit

**Implicit (Cypress-style):** the assertion is a **command** on the queue.

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=status]').should('contain.text', 'Pending');
cy.get('button[type=submit]').should('be.enabled').and('be.visible');
```

`.and` is an alias of `.should` for readability.

**Explicit (Chai-style):** you call `expect` on a **value you already have**.

```ts
cy.request('/api/health').then((resp) => {
  expect(resp.status).to.eq(200);
  expect(resp.body).to.deep.include({ ok: true });
});
```

`expect` does not know how to re-query the DOM. If the value is still "Loading", you fail now.

| | Implicit `.should` | Explicit `expect` |
|---|---|---|
| Retries with `cy.get` | Yes | No (unless inside `.should(fn)`) |
| Reads like Cypress docs | Yes | Yes for HTTP/math |
| BDD chain | `'have.class', 'x'` | `to.have.class('x')` on jQuery |
| Typical use | DOM, URL, intercept from chain | Parsed numbers, plain objects in `.then` |

## Chai, Chai-jQuery, Sinon-Chai

Cypress bundles:

- **Chai** — `expect(1).to.equal(1)`, `assert`, `should` (the Chai object `should`, which you will rarely use as `foo.should.equal` in Cypress — too easy to confuse with `.should()`)
- **Chai-jQuery** — assertions that understand jQuery subjects: `have.class`, `have.attr`, `be.visible`, `be.checked`, `have.length`
- **Sinon-Chai** — `have.been.calledWith` for `cy.stub` / `cy.spy`

Stick to **`cy.*.should('assertion', args)`** for DOM. The string names are Chai-jQuery BDD:

```ts
cy.get('input').should('have.value', 'Ada');
cy.get('input').should('have.attr', 'aria-invalid', 'true');
cy.get('.modal').should('not.exist');
cy.url().should('include', '/leave/');
cy.title().should('eq', 'Leave — Bizlevate HRM');
cy.document().its('readyState').should('eq', 'complete');
```

## Common implicit assertions (HRM cheat sheet)

| Intent | Assertion |
|---|---|
| Visible to a user | `'be.visible'` |
| Gone from DOM | `'not.exist'` |
| Present (maybe hidden) | `'exist'` |
| N matches | `'have.length', n` / `'have.length.at.least', 1` |
| Text | `'contain.text', 'Pending'` / `'have.text', 'Pending'` |
| Class | `'have.class', 'is-selected'` |
| Disabled button | `'be.disabled'` |
| Checkbox | `'be.checked'` |
| URL | `cy.url().should('include', '/payroll')` |

`have.text` is exact (trimmed per Cypress/jQuery rules); `contain.text` is substring. Prefer `contain` for i18n-ish UI; exact when the copy is a contract.

`'exist'` after `cy.get` is often redundant: `get` already retries until the element exists. Prefer `'be.visible'` or a text assertion so you do not pass on a `display:none` node.

## `.should(callback)` — retrying explicit

When Chai-jQuery strings are not enough:

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=balance]').should(($el) => {
  const days = parseInt($el.text(), 10);
  expect(days).to.be.within(0, 30);
});
```

If `expect` throws, Cypress **retries the `get`**. That is how you retry **computed** values.

Rules:

- Throw or fail `expect` to retry
- **Do not** call `cy.*` inside this function
- Keep it fast and side-effect free

## `.then` + `expect` — non-retrying explicit

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=balance]').invoke('text').then((text) => {
  const days = parseInt(text, 10);
  expect(days).to.be.a('number');
});
```

Safe **after** you have already `.should('match', /\d+/)` or equivalent. Otherwise you parse `"--"` once and fail.

HTTP:

```ts
cy.request('GET', '/api/leave').then((res) => {
  expect(res.status).to.eq(200);
  expect(res.body).to.be.an('array');
});
```

Or stay implicit:

```ts
cy.request('GET', '/api/leave')
  .its('status')
  .should('eq', 200);
```

`.its` + `.should` retries `.its` access; for `cy.request` the HTTP call is already done, so retry does not re-hit the network. That is OK for asserting a finished response.

## Negative assertions

```ts
cy.contains('Error').should('not.exist');
```

Negative assertions are easy to get **too fast**: "Error" is not there at t=0, test passes, then an error toast appears. For "no error after submit":

```ts
cy.contains('button', 'Submit').click();
cy.contains('[data-cy=toast]', 'Saved').should('be.visible');
cy.contains('[data-cy=toast]', 'Error').should('not.exist');
```

Assert the **positive** outcome first, then the negative.

## `assert` vs `expect` vs `should`

You may see `assert.equal(a, b)`. Prefer `expect` in `.then` and `.should('...')` on chains. Avoid Chai's `object.should.equal` — it conflicts mentally with Cypress `.should()`.

## Playwright / Selenium

Playwright:

```ts
await expect(page.getByTestId('status')).toHaveText('Pending');
expect(body.ok).toBe(true); // generic, no retry
```

Locator expects retry; generic `expect` does not. Same split as Cypress should vs expect.

Selenium: `Assert.assertEquals` — never waits. Always wrap with `WebDriverWait` if the DOM is async.

## TS notes

Chai-jQuery types come from the Cypress package. If `'be.visible'` errors, your `cypress/tsconfig.json` `types` array is wrong (Part 1.8).

Custom assertion messages:

```ts
cy.get('tr').should((($rows) => {
  expect($rows.length, 'leave rows after seed').to.eq(3);
}) as any); // prefer should('have.length', 3)
```

Keep it simple: `should('have.length', 3)`.

## HRM combined example

```ts
it('manager sees three pending leaves', () => {
  cy.visit('/leave?filter=pending');
  cy.get('[data-cy=leave-table] tbody tr')
    .should('have.length', 3)
    .and('be.visible')
    .each(($row) => {
      cy.wrap($row).should('contain.text', 'Pending');
    });
});
```

`each` + `cy.wrap` leads into the next chapter: **`cy.wrap` six uses**.
## `.and` chains are still one retry unit

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=submit]')
  .should('be.visible')
  .and('be.enabled')
  .and('contain.text', 'Submit');
```

All three must pass; Cypress retries the command as a bundle. If you need "visible now, enabled later," split into two commands (usually unnecessary).

## `should('not.exist')` vs `should('not.be.visible')`

| Assertion | DOM node |
|---|---|
| `not.exist` | No matching node |
| `not.be.visible` | Node may exist but hidden |

A closed modal might remain in the DOM (`not.be.visible`) or be unmounted (`not.exist`). Assert what the framework does. HRM React often unmounts.

## Multiple subjects and `.should('have.length')`

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=chip]').should('have.length', 3);
```

Retries until 3 chips. `eq(3)` is the 4th element (0-based) and will retry existence of that index — different meaning.

## Asserting the URL after submit

```ts
cy.contains('button', 'Submit').click();
cy.location('pathname').should('match', /\/leave\/lv_/);
cy.contains('[data-cy=toast]', 'submitted').should('be.visible');
```

`cy.url()` returns the full URL string. `cy.hash()`, `cy.location('search')` are siblings. All retry.

## Chai `deep.equal` vs `deep.include`

```ts
expect(body).to.deep.equal({ ok: true });       // exact keys
expect(body).to.deep.include({ ok: true });     // subset
cy.wrap(body).should('deep.include', { ok: true });
```

API bodies grow fields; `include` is kinder. Snapshots of entire payloads flake.

## Interview drill

Should vs expect — which retries? Show a should(fn). Why is expect in `.then` flaky for DOM? Name three Chai-jQuery assertions you use on a button.
## Table: pick the assertion

| You want to know | Write |
|---|---|
| Button can be pressed | `.should('be.enabled').and('be.visible')` |
| Table finished loading | `.should('have.length', n)` or intercept wait + length |
| Copy contract | `.should('contain.text', 'Pending')` |
| Attribute | `.should('have.attr', 'href', '/leave/new')` |
| HTTP status | `.its('status').should('eq', 200)` or `expect(res.status).to.eq(200)` in then |
| Parsed number | `.should(($el) => { expect(parseInt($el.text(), 10)).to.be.gt(0); })` |

## `assert` from Chai

```ts
cy.get('tr').then(($tr) => {
  assert.isAbove($tr.length, 0);
});
```

Still non-retrying. Team style: `should` on DOM, `expect` in then for HTTP. Skip `assert` unless you like it.

## Sinon-Chai (preview)

```ts
cy.window().then((win) => {
  cy.stub(win.console, 'error').as('consoleError');
});
cy.visit('/leave');
cy.get('@consoleError').should('not.have.been.called');
```

`have.been.called` is Sinon-Chai. The stub alias is a **data/sinon** alias, not DOM. Part 7 covers stubs; know assertions exist.

## Soft vs hard

Cypress does not have Playwright's `expect.soft`. One failed `should` stops the test. That is OK. Do not wrap everything in try/catch.

## Interview closer

"Implicit `should` retries with the query. Explicit `expect` does not, unless I put it in `should(fn)`. I never `expect` in the `it` body before the queue runs."
## `should('have.value')` vs `invoke('val')`

```ts
cy.get('#email').should('have.value', 'ada@bizlevate.test');
```

Retries until the input shows that value (useful after autofill). `invoke('val').then(expect)` does not retry. Same lesson, form fields edition.

## `include` vs `eq` on URLs

```ts
cy.url().should('include', '/leave/');     // extra query string OK
cy.location('pathname').should('eq', '/leave/new'); // exact path
```

HRM often adds `?tab=`. `include` on full URL still works; `pathname` + `eq` is stricter.

## Chai `throw`

```ts
expect(() => JSON.parse('nope')).to.throw();
```

Explicit, no retry, no DOM. Fine in `.then` after `cy.readFile`.
## `and('have.focus')` after type

```ts
cy.get('#email').type('ada@bizlevate.test').should('have.value', 'ada@bizlevate.test');
```

Value assertion retries until typing finished and React re-rendered. `expect(el.val())` in a `then` right after `type` can still see the previous value. Implicit wins on form fields.

## `not.be.disabled` vs `be.enabled`

Prefer `'be.enabled'` for controls. Some elements are not disabled but also not enabled in the Chai-jQuery sense (non-form nodes). Assert on `button`/`input`.

## Deep equal flake

```ts
cy.request('/api/leave/lv_1').its('body').should('deep.equal', entireSnapshot);
```

The API adds `updatedAt`. Use `deep.include` for the fields you own (`status`, `employeeId`) or `expect(body.status).to.eq('PENDING')` in then after the request finished (HTTP does not need retry).
## `should('match', regex)` on invoke text

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=balance]').invoke('text').should('match', /\d+\s*days/i);
```

Retries until the text matches. Equivalent to `should(($el) => expect($el.text()).to.match(...))` with less code. Prefer this over `then` + `expect`.
## Chai-jQuery `contain` vs `include` vs `have.text`

```ts
cy.get('[data-cy=status]').should('contain', 'Pending');      // substring, DOM text
cy.get('[data-cy=status]').should('include.text', 'Pending'); // similar
cy.get('[data-cy=status]').should('have.text', 'Pending');    // exact
```

`contain`/`include.text` retry until the substring appears (loading skeleton → Pending). `have.text` retries until exact equality — extra whitespace fails. Start with `contain.text` for HRM chips.

## `expect` in phase 1 is always wrong for the DOM

```ts
it('wrong', () => {
  expect(Cypress.$('h1').text()).to.eq('Sign in'); // page not visited yet
});
```

Phase 1 runs before `visit`. Explicit assertions belong **inside** `.then` after a command, or better, be rewritten as implicit `should`.


## Default Chai `equal` vs `eq`

`.should('eq', 200)` and `.should('equal', 200)` are Chai aliases. Cypress docs use `eq` heavily. `eql` is deep equality for objects — prefer `deep.equal` / `deep.include` by name so readers know it is deep.

## Retry budget

Every implicit assertion spends up to `defaultCommandTimeout`. A spec with twenty `should('exist')` lines can still be fast when they pass on the first try. They get expensive when selectors are wrong. Unique `data-cy` plus one strong assertion beats five weak ones that each retry 4s on failure.

chapters.title: 2.7 cy.wrap()
chapters.overviewText: cy.wrap(value) puts an arbitrary value onto the Cypress command queue so you can .should, .its, .then, or alias it. The six uses you must be able to list: wrap a primitive, wrap a plain object, wrap a Promise, wrap jQuery/DOM nodes (especially in .each), yield a value from a custom command, and re-wrap inside .then so a following .should can retry. wrap is not a query — it does not find elements in the document by selector.
chapters.why: Without wrap, .each, custom commands, and Promise interop fall off the queue. With wrap misused, people think wrap('#id') queries the DOM (it does not). Interviews often ask for several wrap use cases, not just one.
chapters.when: Inside .each, when asserting a leftover JS value, when a plugin returns a Promise, when writing Commands.add that must yield, and when bridging .then to a retrying .should.

practical.scenario: For each leave row, assert status text; plus assert a computed remaining-days number; plus wrap a Promise from a small helper that reads Cypress.env.
practical.pass: You cy.get('tr').each(($row) => { cy.wrap($row).find('[data-cy=status]').should('be.visible'); }); you wrap primitives/objects/promises; you do not cy.wrap('[data-cy=status]') expecting a query.
practical.fail: You cy.wrap('tbody tr') hoping it acts like cy.get, or you skip wrap in each and call $row.find as if Cypress would retry it.

chapters.customSummary:
- cy.wrap(x) yields x on the queue — it is not cy.get(x).
- Six uses: (1) primitive for should/expect, (2) plain object + its/should, (3) Promise so Cypress waits, (4) jQuery/DOM in .each or callbacks, (5) yield from custom commands, (6) re-wrap in .then to continue a retrying should.
- Wrapped DOM/jQuery + should can retry commands on that subject; wrapped snapshots may not re-query the live document — prefer cy.get for page elements.
- Return null from tasks; wrap in the browser for Chainable APIs.
- Playwright does not need wrap — you already hold values with await. Selenium neither.
